We use **banker's rounding**, `decimal.ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, and never `ROUND_HALF_UP`. Tax is rounded on each line item separately, and those rounded line taxes are then added up. The invoice total is never rounded.

This rule isn't written anywhere in the code yet. It comes from the project's memory store, which says it was agreed with the finance team in March 2026 after customers reported invoices that were off by a cent.

The code has nothing to check it against. `tax_for(amount_cents, rate)` in `src/billing/tax.py:11` just raises `NotImplementedError`, and nothing in `src/` rounds anything.

A related rule from the same store: all money amounts are integer cents using the `Money` type in `src/billing/money.py`. Floats aren't used for money, not even for intermediate math. So when `tax_for` gets written, it should do the math in `Decimal`, round each line half-even to whole cents, and return an integer.
